items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1959-03-18
items.q: INTERVIEWER: I knew of Emil Begard. That was Barney Sunko on violin. [INTERVIEWEE] No, this was a trumpet player, Homer Begard.

ctx.x: Yeah, well, yeah, he used the book. You see, after I left Walter Defining, well, you know, I went to Louie. Louie, there were some things that I had the wrong understanding about the division, and Louie straightened me out on that. And, well, I got out of work. I wasn't paying much, but I got out of work. So I thought, I said, well, Louie, I'm not coming for lessons right now because I'm not working. I won't be able to pay you. He said, well, that don't stop you from coming. I said, well, no, I don't want to be…
I knew of Emil Begard. That was Barney Sunko on violin.
No, this was a trumpet player, Homer Begard. I don't remember.
